answers.label: Q.1
answers.solution:
Pure alcohol in 400 ml of a \(15\%\) solution \(= \frac{15}{100} \times 400 = 60\) ml.
Let \(x\) ml of pure alcohol be added. Alcohol becomes \((60 + x)\) ml in \((400 + x)\) ml of solution.
\(\frac{60 + x}{400 + x} = \frac{32}{100}\)
\(100(60 + x) = 32(400 + x)\)
\(6000 + 100x = 12800 + 32x\)
\(68x = 6800\), so \(x = 100\)
Check: \(\frac{160}{500} = 32\%\).
So, 100 ml of pure alcohol must be added.

Let the number of 10 paise coins be \(x\).
25 paise coins \(= 3x\); 50 paise coins \(= 3x + 5\).
Total value in paise: \(10x + 25(3x) + 50(3x + 5) = 12000\) (Rs 120 = 12000 paise)
\(10x + 75x + 150x + 250 = 12000\)
\(235x = 11750\)
\(x = 50\)
Check: 50 coins of 10 p = Rs 5, 150 coins of 25 p = Rs 37.50, 155 coins of 50 p = Rs 77.50; total Rs 120.
So, there are 50 coins of 10 paise.

answers.solution:
He charges for 1000 g but gives only 950 g, at cost price.
So for goods costing him the price of 950 g, he receives the price of 1000 g.
Gain \(= 1000 - 950 = 50\) g (in value).
Gain \(\% = \frac{50}{950} \times 100 = \frac{100}{19} = 5\frac{5}{19}\%\)
So, his gain is \(5\frac{5}{19}\%\) (about \(5.26\%\)).

answers.label: Q.5
answers.solution:
Numerator: \(x^{m+n} \times x^{n+l} \times x^{l+m} = x^{(m+n)+(n+l)+(l+m)} = x^{2m+2n+2l}\)
Denominator: \(x^m \times x^n \times x^l = x^{m+n+l}\)
\(\frac{x^{2m+2n+2l}}{x^{m+n+l}} = x^{2m+2n+2l-(m+n+l)} = x^{m+n+l}\)
So, the expression simplifies to \(x^{m+n+l}\).

The four arcs meet at the mid-points of the sides, so each arc has radius \(\frac{14}{2} = 7\) cm.
Each arc is drawn at a corner of the square, so it is a quarter circle (\(90^\circ\)).

Simplify the surds first: \(\sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}\), \(\sqrt{27} = 3\sqrt{3}\), \(\sqrt{48} = 4\sqrt{3}\).
First part: \(5\sqrt{3}(3\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{3}) = 5\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3} = 15\)
Second part: \(2\sqrt{3}(4 \times 3\sqrt{3} - 5 \times 4\sqrt{3}) = 2\sqrt{3}(12\sqrt{3} - 20\sqrt{3}) = 2\sqrt{3} \times (-8\sqrt{3}) = -48\)
Total \(= 15 + (-48) = -33\)
So, the value is \(-33\).

answers.label: Q.9
answers.solution:
The figure is cut off at the bottom: the labels B and C are not visible. Take B as the bottom-left vertex of the triangle and BC as the horizontal line through it, so the \(125^\circ\) angle is between BC (going left) and BA (A is the top vertex).
Angle between BA and the horizontal on the right \(= 180^\circ - 125^\circ = 55^\circ\).
At D, \(\angle ADE = 112^\circ\), so the angle between DA and the horizontal on the left \(= 180^\circ - 112^\circ = 68^\circ\).
Draw a line through A parallel to BC and DE.
Alternate angles: the angle at A on the left side of AB \(= 55^\circ\), and on the right side of AD \(= 68^\circ\).
Angles on a straight line at A: \(55^\circ + x + 68^\circ = 180^\circ\)
\(x = 180^\circ - 123^\circ = 57^\circ\)
(Equivalently, the exterior angle \(112^\circ = x + 55^\circ\).)
So, \(x = 57^\circ\).

answers.label: Q.10
answers.finalAnswer: Heights of the girls of Class X (number of girls in each height group); 140-145 cm; 70%; 145-150 cm
answers.solution:
Note: the axis labels are hard to read; the class intervals are taken as equal steps of 5 cm ending at 160 cm: 125-130, 130-135, 135-140, 140-145, 145-150, 150-155, 155-160. The question numbers (iii) then (vi) are printed for (iii), (iv).
From the bars: 125-130: 1, 130-135: 2, 135-140: 3, 140-145: 7, 145-150: 4, 150-155: 2, 155-160: 1. Total \(= 20\) girls.
(i) The graph shows the heights (in cm) of the girls of Class X: how many girls fall in each height group.
(ii) The tallest bar is 7, for the group 140-145 cm, so that group contains the most girls.
(iii) Girls of height 140 cm and above \(= 7 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 14\). Percentage \(= \frac{14}{20} \times 100 = 70\%\).
(iv) \(20\%\) of 20 girls \(= 4\) girls, which is the group 145-150 cm.
So, the answers are: (i) heights of girls of Class X, (ii) 140-145 cm, (iii) \(70\%\), (iv) 145-150 cm.

answers.label: Q.11
answers.solution:
The four long lines form a quadrilateral in the middle, and at each corner of it a small triangle sticks out.
In each small triangle, the third angle (at the corner of the quadrilateral) is vertically opposite to that interior angle of the quadrilateral.
So \(p + q = 180^\circ - \angle 1\), \(r + s = 180^\circ - \angle 2\), \(t + u = 180^\circ - \angle 3\), \(v + w = 180^\circ - \angle 4\), where \(\angle 1, \angle 2, \angle 3, \angle 4\) are the angles of the quadrilateral.
Adding: \(p + q + r + s + t + u + v + w = 4 \times 180^\circ - (\angle 1 + \angle 2 + \angle 3 + \angle 4)\)
\(= 720^\circ - 360^\circ = 360^\circ\)
So, the sum is \(360^\circ\).

Cost of 25 kg at Rs 4 per kg \(= 25 \times 4 = \text{Rs } 100\)
Cost of 35 kg at Rs 4.50 per kg \(= 35 \times 4.50 = \text{Rs } 157.50\)
Total cost of 60 kg \(= 100 + 157.50 = \text{Rs } 257.50\)
Selling price of 60 kg at Rs 4.50 per kg \(= 60 \times 4.50 = \text{Rs } 270\)
Profit \(= 270 - 257.50 = \text{Rs } 12.50\)
So, he makes a profit of Rs 12.50.

\(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{4}{9} + \frac{2}{7} = \frac{21}{126} + \frac{56}{126} + \frac{36}{126} = \frac{113}{126}\)
The additive inverse of a number is the number which added to it gives 0.
So, the additive inverse is \(-\frac{113}{126}\).

Area of trapezium \(= \frac{1}{2} \times (\text{sum of parallel sides}) \times \text{height}\)
\(306 = \frac{1}{2} \times (7x + 11x) \times 17\)
\(306 = 9x \times 17 = 153x\)
\(x = 2\)
Parallel sides \(= 7 \times 2 = 14\) cm and \(11 \times 2 = 22\) cm.
So, the parallel sides are 14 cm and 22 cm.

Total cost of 3 fans \(= 3 \times 450 = \text{Rs } 1350\)
For a \(20\%\) gain, total selling price \(= \frac{120}{100} \times 1350 = \text{Rs } 1620\)
One fan sold at \(10\%\) loss: SP \(= \frac{90}{100} \times 450 = \text{Rs } 405\)
SP needed for the other two \(= 1620 - 405 = \text{Rs } 1215\)
Each of the two \(= \frac{1215}{2} = \text{Rs } 607.50\)
So, the other two must be sold for Rs 1215 in all, that is Rs 607.50 each.

Pass marks \(= 42\%\) of \(M - 28\) (Dayne got 28 more than the pass mark)

answers.solution:
The angles to find are the marked angles \(x\), \(y\) and \(z\).
The \(120^\circ\) angle is at the point where line \(f\) (falling to the right) meets line \(a\) (horizontal), between \(f\) going up and \(a\) going right.
So the angle between \(f\) going down and \(a\) going right \(= 180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ\) (angles on a straight line).
\(x\): \(c\) is parallel to \(f\), and \(x\) is the angle between \(a\) (going right) and \(c\) (going down to the right). It corresponds to the \(60^\circ\) angle, so \(x = 60^\circ\).
\(z\): at the bottom-right corner, between \(d\) (going left) and \(f\) (going up to the left). Since \(a \parallel d\), \(z\) is the alternate angle to the \(60^\circ\) angle at the top, so \(z = 60^\circ\).
\(y\): where \(c\) crosses \(d\), between \(d\) going left and \(c\) going down. The angle between \(d\) going right and \(c\) going down is \(60^\circ\) (corresponding, since \(c \parallel f\)), so \(y = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ\).
So, \(x = 60^\circ\), \(y = 120^\circ\), \(z = 60^\circ\). (Every point of the star is \(60^\circ\).)

answers.label: Q.23
answers.solution:
\(\left(\frac{x^m}{x^n}\right)^l = x^{l(m-n)} = x^{lm - ln}\)
\(\left(\frac{x^n}{x^l}\right)^m = x^{m(n-l)} = x^{mn - ml}\)
\(\left(\frac{x^l}{x^m}\right)^n = x^{n(l-m)} = x^{nl - nm}\)
Multiply by adding the powers:
\(lm - ln + mn - ml + nl - nm = 0\)
So the product \(= x^0 = 1\).
So, the value is 1.

Let the length of the train be \(L\) m. To cross a bridge, the train covers (its length + the bridge's length).
Speed \(= \frac{L + 300}{15} = \frac{L + 450}{21}\)
\(21(L + 300) = 15(L + 450)\)
\(21L + 6300 = 15L + 6750\)
\(6L = 450\), so \(L = 75\) m
Speed \(= \frac{75 + 300}{15} = \frac{375}{15} = 25\) m/s
In km/hr: \(25 \times \frac{18}{5} = 90\) km/hr
(Check: \(\frac{525}{21} = 25\) m/s.)
So, the speed is 90 km/hr and the train is 75 m long.

\(2x + 4 = 4(x - 6)\)
\(2x + 4 = 4x - 24\)
\(2x = 28\), so \(x = 14\)
Present ages: Shyam 14 years, Karthik 28 years.
(Check: \(28 + 4 = 32 = 4 \times (14 - 6)\).)
Two years ago: Shyam \(14 - 2 = 12\) years, Karthik \(28 - 2 = 26\) years.
So, two years ago Shyam was 12 and Karthik was 26.

2 men do the same work as 3 women, so 1 man \(= \frac{3}{2}\) women.
4 men \(= 4 \times \frac{3}{2} = 6\) women.
4 men and 9 women \(= 6 + 9 = 15\) women.
3 women take 40 hours, so the work is \(3 \times 40 = 120\) woman-hours.
Time for 15 women \(= \frac{120}{15} = 8\) hours
So, they will take 8 hours.

answers.label: Q.28
answers.solution:
The rectangle is 28 cm by 14 cm. The unshaded semicircle stands on the 14 cm side, so its radius is 7 cm.
Area of rectangle \(= 28 \times 14 = 392\text{ cm}^2\)
Area of semicircle \(= \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = 77\text{ cm}^2\)
Shaded area \(= 392 - 77 = 315\text{ cm}^2\)
Perimeter of the shaded region = top side + right side + bottom side + curved edge of the semicircle (the left side is the semicircle's diameter and is not on the shaded boundary).
Curved edge \(= \pi r = \frac{22}{7} \times 7 = 22\) cm
Perimeter \(= 28 + 14 + 28 + 22 = 92\) cm
So, the shaded area is \(315\text{ cm}^2\) and its perimeter is 92 cm.

answers.solution:
Let the polygons have \(n\) and \(2n\) sides.
Interior angle of the first \(= \frac{(n - 2) \times 180^\circ}{n}\)
Interior angle of the second \(= \frac{(2n - 2) \times 180^\circ}{2n} = \frac{(n - 1) \times 180^\circ}{n}\)
Ratio: \(\frac{n - 2}{n - 1} = \frac{3}{4}\)
\(4(n - 2) = 3(n - 1)\)
\(4n - 8 = 3n - 3\)
\(n = 5\)
Check: a pentagon's angle is \(108^\circ\), a decagon's \(144^\circ\), and \(108 : 144 = 3 : 4\).
So, the polygons have 5 and 10 sides.
